about: What a locked-down tool looks like on a machine that uses the Consus Launcher. The launcher embeds this file and renders it into each tool's user-space settings; the Consus portal renders the same values into the device-management lock files. Values only. How a value reaches the disk (merging, helper links, model discovery) lives in code. A key an app does not know is ignored by that app version. Keys are nested objects; a renderer that needs dotted paths flattens them. A tool with `extends` takes every field it does not set from the tool it extends.

endpoint.note: The org's gateway root, no trailing slash; the Anthropic-compatible surface. From the EndpointURL org setting, default https://api.consus.io.

helper.note: The credential helper, as a plain path: the launcher's keychain helper (default) or the Consus credential helper script.

helper_shell.note: The same helper as a command a shell runs; a path with a space is quoted.

model.note: The tool's starting model at the org's compliance level, from the gateway's /v1/models.

models.note: Every model the key may use at that level, in the tool's own list shape.

background.note: Claude Code's background model; never Sonnet 5 (no structured outputs through the gateway).

context_window.note: Claude Code's context window as a decimal string; omitted when 200000 or less.

endpoint_host.note: The host of endpoint, for allowlists.

claude-desktop.name: Claude Desktop
claude-desktop.file: Claude Desktop's third-party (gateway) configuration: a config-library entry in user space, or the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop managed profile.

lock.note: Every value is a string in a profile or the registry; arrays, objects and booleans are JSON encoded as strings.

readme.telemetry: Off: crash and error reports, analytics, model catalog, connector icons, previews, auto-update
readme.leaves_machine: Sandbox VM bundle from `downloads.claude.ai` at the first Cowork or Code session

claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.file: Claude Code's settings.json: the launcher's profile in user space, or the machine-wide managed-settings.json.

lock.note: Values under env must be strings.

readme.telemetry: Off: analytics, error reports, feature flags, update checks, plugin marketplace, WebFetch domain check, sign-in paths
readme.shell: None / any host on macOS, and on Linux with `bubblewrap` and `socat` (Claude Code's sandbox); not restricted on Windows
readme.leaves_machine: Nothing measured (2.1.307, through a logging proxy)
readme.lock: `managed-settings.json` from the portal, which can also carry `allowedProviders` and `allowManagedDomainsOnly`

chatgpt-desktop.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt-desktop.file: ~/.codex/config.toml, shared with the user's own Codex CLI; the lock is Codex's requirements.toml.
chatgpt-desktop.toml:
# ChatGPT desktop app (and Codex CLI): ~/.codex/config.toml, merged key by key.
# Verbatim from the Consus integration guide for ChatGPT desktop, except the
# key: env_http_headers instead of an inline http_headers, so it never lands in
# the file. Docs checked: that guide and the Consus portal's Codex template,
# 2026-09-22. Verified on a real machine: macOS,
# ChatGPT 26.915, 2026-09-22. The model line is added by chatgpt.rs.
# Top-level keys must stay above the first [table] header.

model_provider = "consus"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium"
model_reasoning_summary = "auto"
web_search = "disabled"
approval_policy = "on-request"
approvals_reviewer = "user"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"

# network_access follows the org's WebAccess setting (chatgpt.rs); this is
# the closed value.
[sandbox_workspace_write]
network_access = false

[model_providers.consus]
name = "Consus Gateway"
base_url = "https://api.consus.io/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
env_http_headers = { "x-api-key" = "CONSUS_API_KEY" }

[shell_environment_policy]
inherit = "all"
exclude = ["AWS_*", "AZURE_*", "GOOGLE_*", "GCP_*", "CONSUS_*", "OPENAI_*", "ANTHROPIC_*", "*_KEY", "*_TOKEN", "*_SECRET", "*PASSWORD*"]

[features]
computer_use = false
browser_use = false
browser_use_external = false
browser_use_full_cdp_access = false
in_app_browser = false
image_generation = false
realtime_conversation = false
in_app_dictation = false
apps = false
remote_plugin = false
plugin_sharing = false
recommended_plugins = false
tool_suggest = false
skill_mcp_dependency_install = false
memories = false

[computer_use]
default_app_access = "deny"

[browser_use]
allow_history_access = false

[browser_use.default_origin_policy]
access = "deny"
uploads = "deny"
downloads = "deny"
full_cdp_access = "deny"

[memories]
use_memories = false
generate_memories = false

[analytics]
enabled = false

[feedback]
enabled = false

[otel]
exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
log_user_prompt = false

lock_only.requirements_toml:
allowed_approval_policies = ["untrusted", "on-request"]
allowed_approvals_reviewers = ["user"]
allowed_sandbox_modes = ["read-only", "workspace-write"]
allowed_web_search_modes = []
allow_appshots = false
allow_remote_control = false

default_permissions = ":workspace"

[allowed_permission_profiles]
":read-only" = true
":workspace" = true

[features]
computer_use = false
browser_use = false
browser_use_external = false
browser_use_full_cdp_access = false
in_app_browser = false
image_generation = false
realtime_conversation = false
in_app_dictation = false
apps = false
remote_plugin = false
plugin_sharing = false
memories = false

[computer_use]
default_app_access = "deny"
allow_persistent_approval = false
allow_locked_computer_use = false

[browser_use]
allow_history_access = false
allow_global_persistent_approval = false

[browser_use.default_origin_policy]
access = "deny"

[marketplaces]
restrict_to_allowed_sources = true

[permissions.filesystem]
deny_read = ["/**/*.env", "~/.ssh", "~/.aws", "~/.azure", "~/.config/gcloud", "~/.kube"]

[experimental_network]
enabled = true
managed_allowed_domains_only = true

[experimental_network.domains]
"{{endpoint_host}}" = "allow"

lock.note: Also governs the Codex CLI on the same machine. web_search stays "disabled" in config.toml under either web-access value: it is OpenAI's hosted tool, which the gateway strips.

readme.telemetry: Off in the agent: analytics, feedback upload, OpenTelemetry export. The app around it keeps OpenAI's own update and product-analytics connections
readme.web_search: Off in the file; the gateway strips it if turned back on
readme.leaves_machine: The app's own connections to OpenAI

codex-cli.name: Codex CLI
codex-cli.file: config.toml in the launcher's own Codex profile; the same lock as ChatGPT.

readme.telemetry: Off: analytics, feedback, OpenTelemetry export, update check

pi.name: Pi
pi.file: Environment of the Pi process the launcher starts; Pi has no managed settings and no lock.

readme.shell: Not restricted: Pi has no sandbox
readme.leaves_machine: `fd` and `ripgrep` from GitHub on first run
readme.lock: Pi offers no lock; a container or the network edge
